name: Hall Complement-Section Obstruction Tower
definition: Let $H\subseteq Q_{12}$ be Hall's 299-concept cornerless maximum class, let $K_0=Q_{12}\setminus H$, and use the resolving tips $183,315,1836$. For $r\ge0$, put $K=K_0\times Q_r$ on $12+r$ new coordinates. In the common-seed construction, place $K$ at tip 183 and the two oppositely punctured $(12+r)$-cubes at tips 315 and 1836; call the resulting family $X_r$.
parameters: $r\ge0$; $X_r$ has isometric dimension $24+r$ and order $1{,}236{,}693\cdot2^r-2$. For $r=0$, its order is $1{,}236{,}691$ and its cube complement has order $15{,}540{,}525$.
properties: Every $X_r$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor. The section of its cube complement at old word 183 is $H\times Q_r$, which is nonpeelable, so the entire complement is nonpeelable. Therefore $X_r$ cannot be reached from its ambient cube by corner deletions. The large outputs are specified by the construction and are not enumerated.
